questions.stem: A security team connects a new sensor to a switch SPAN port and configures it to drop exploit traffic. Attacks still reach the servers. What is the cause?
options: The sensor needs Snort 3 instead of Snort 2
A SPAN-fed sensor only receives a copy of traffic, so it can alert but never block
SPAN ports cannot carry encrypted traffic
The intrusion policy is set to Balanced Security and Connectivity
questions.explanation: Only an inline device can drop the original packet. A sensor on a SPAN port gets a copy after the real packet has already been forwarded, so it behaves as an IDS no matter how its policy is set.

questions.stem: An engineer wants to evaluate a new FTD intrusion policy on a production link and see what it would block, with zero risk of dropping traffic. Which interface configuration fits?
options: Routed interfaces with the policy in Maximum Detection
Inline set with tap mode enabled
questions.explanation: An inline set in tap mode sits physically in the path but only copies traffic to Snort, so it can never drop anything. After tuning, tap mode is turned off and the same inline set starts blocking.

questions.stem: NGFW inspection must be added between a server VLAN and its existing default gateway. Server and router IP addresses cannot change. Which firewall mode meets the requirement?
questions.explanation: Transparent mode makes the firewall a Layer 2 bump in the wire: interfaces join a bridge group and the management IP lives on the BVI. Hosts keep their gateway, yet full access control and IPS still apply.

questions.stem: Which two statements about Cisco Secure Firewall Threat Defense high availability are true?
options: FTD supports active/active failover with failover groups
FTD clustering lets several units act as one logical firewall
FTD high availability requires multiple context mode
FTD failover requires the units to run different software versions
questions.explanation: FTD failover is active/standby only, and clustering combines units into one logical device for scale and resiliency. Active/active failover is an ASA feature that depends on multiple context mode.

questions.stem: Which capability is built into FTD but was never native to the classic ASA software?
questions.explanation: ASA is a stateful firewall with NAT and VPN. Snort IPS, application visibility, URL filtering and malware defense are built into FTD. On ASA they needed the old FirePOWER add-on module, which is end-of-life.

questions.stem: A company needs to manage forty FTD devices from one console and wants that console delivered as SaaS. Which option fits best?
options: Cloud-delivered Firewall Management Center in Security Cloud Control
A local FMCv on every site
questions.explanation: FDM manages a single FTD and ASDM manages a single ASA. Cloud-delivered FMC, part of Cisco Security Cloud Control (formerly CDO), manages many FTDs from the cloud.

questions.stem: Remote employees work from home and cafes without VPN. Security wants firewall and IPS policy applied to their internet traffic with no hardware involved. Which Cisco solution fits?
options: FTDv in a private data center
questions.explanation: Cisco Secure Access is the cloud-delivered SSE platform. Its cloud firewall with IPS, SWG and DNS-layer security follow the user wherever they connect, with traffic steered by Cisco Secure Client.

questions.stem: Workloads run in AWS and Azure. The team wants cloud-native, SaaS-managed gateways to control ingress, egress and east-west traffic across both clouds. Which product is designed for this?
questions.explanation: Multicloud Defense deploys SaaS-managed gateways inside customer cloud accounts for ingress, egress and east-west protection. Secure Network Analytics is NDR (visibility), not enforcement.

questions.stem: On an IOS XE router, interfaces G0/0 (zone INSIDE) and G0/1 (zone OUTSIDE) have a zone-pair with an inspect policy. G0/2 was never assigned to a zone. What happens to traffic from G0/2 to G0/0?
options: It is permitted because G0/2 has no policy
It is inspected by the INSIDE-OUTSIDE zone-pair
It is dropped because traffic between a zone member and a non-zone interface is never allowed
questions.explanation: With ZBFW, an interface in a zone cannot exchange traffic with an interface that is in no zone. Assign G0/2 to a zone and create a zone-pair to allow it.

questions.stem: A ZBFW policy uses the pass action from INSIDE to DMZ. Users report that requests reach the DMZ server but replies never come back. Why?
options: pass drops packets after the first one
pass is stateless and one-way, so a mirror rule from DMZ to INSIDE is needed for return traffic
questions.explanation: inspect is stateful and allows return traffic automatically. pass is stateless and unidirectional, so return traffic needs its own rule or the action should be inspect.

questions.stem: Which two methods let an NGFW detect threats inside TLS-encrypted sessions?
options: Decryption policy with Decrypt-Resign for outbound traffic
Encrypted Visibility Engine fingerprinting of the TLS handshake
Increasing the Snort rule update frequency
Moving the sensor to a SPAN port
questions.explanation: Decryption gives full payload visibility at a performance and privacy cost. The Encrypted Visibility Engine identifies applications and malware from the TLS ClientHello without decrypting. Rule updates and SPAN placement do nothing for encrypted payloads.

questions.stem: Which FTD base intrusion policy is the recommended starting point for most production deployments?
questions.explanation: Balanced Security and Connectivity is Cisco's recommended default. Maximum Detection enables nearly everything and is meant for testing, not production.

questions.stem: An IPS blocks a legitimate payroll application every month-end. What is this event called?
questions.explanation: A false positive is the IPS firing on benign traffic. Here it causes an outage. A false negative is the opposite: an attack the IPS misses.

questions.stem: Which detection method blocks traffic to a known command-and-control IP before deep packet inspection takes place on FTD?
options: Signature matching in the network analysis policy
questions.explanation: Security Intelligence uses Talos reputation feeds and is evaluated early, before deep inspection, so known-bad IPs, URLs and domains are dropped cheaply.

questions.stem: A branch has no room or budget for a separate firewall. Which two Cisco options provide firewall and IPS functions at the branch?
options: IOS XE Zone-Based Firewall with Snort IPS on the branch router
questions.explanation: IOS XE routers can run ZBFW plus Snort IPS in a UTD container, and Meraki MX is a cloud-managed branch firewall with Snort-based IDS/IPS. Flow Sensor and Telemetry Broker are visibility tools; SNMPv3 is management.

questions.stem: Management insists that the internet link must stay up even if the inline IPS engine crashes. Which behaviour should be configured?
options: Fail-open, for example Snort fail-open or hardware bypass
questions.explanation: Fail-open keeps forwarding traffic uninspected when inspection fails, favouring availability. Fail-closed stops traffic, favouring security. It is a business choice.

questions.stem: A router is configured with `logging trap 4`. Which messages are sent to the syslog server?
questions.explanation: The configured level includes itself and every more severe level, and lower numbers are more severe. Level 4 (warnings) therefore sends 0 through 4.

questions.stem: Auditors require that syslog messages cannot be read or modified in transit. What should be used?
options: Syslog over UDP 514 with a higher severity level
questions.explanation: Classic syslog on UDP 514 is cleartext. Secure syslog runs over TLS, normally on TCP 6514, giving confidentiality and integrity.

questions.stem: Which SNMPv3 security level provides both authentication and encryption?
questions.explanation: authPriv uses HMAC (SHA) for authentication and AES or 3DES for privacy. authNoPriv authenticates but leaves the payload readable.

questions.stem: The NMS team must be sure every critical device notification is received, even across a lossy WAN. Which SNMP mechanism should they use?
questions.explanation: Informs are acknowledged by the manager and retransmitted until confirmed. Traps are fire-and-forget.

questions.stem: Which two statements about NetFlow and IPFIX are correct?
options: IPFIX is the IETF standard derived from NetFlow v9
NetFlow v5 supports IPv6 flow records
NetFlow records include the full packet payload
questions.explanation: NetFlow v9 introduced templates, which made it extensible, and IPFIX standardised that design (default UDP 4739). v5 is fixed and IPv4-only, and no NetFlow version carries payload.

questions.stem: In Flexible NetFlow, which component defines the key fields that decide which packets belong to the same flow?
questions.explanation: The flow record holds match statements (key fields) and collect statements (non-key fields). The exporter says where to send, and the monitor ties a record to an exporter and is applied to an interface.

questions.stem: Which technology lets an ASA or FTD report flow-create, flow-teardown and flow-denied events, including NAT translations, as NetFlow v9 records?
questions.explanation: NetFlow Secure Event Logging (NSEL) exports firewall connection events as NetFlow v9. eStreamer streams FMC events, ERSPAN mirrors packets, and pxGrid shares identity context.

questions.stem: An IDS sensor sits in the data center, three routed hops away from the access switch whose traffic must be monitored. Which mirroring method should be used?
questions.explanation: ERSPAN GRE-encapsulates mirrored traffic so it can cross a Layer 3 network. RSPAN only spans Layer 2 switches using an RSPAN VLAN.

questions.stem: An operations team wants interface counters from 500 switches every 10 seconds, with less device CPU load than today's SNMP polling. What should they deploy?
questions.explanation: Streaming telemetry pushes structured YANG data periodically or on change. It scales far better than polling and costs the device less CPU.

questions.stem: In model-driven telemetry, what is a dial-out subscription?
options: The collector connects to the device and subscribes with NETCONF
The device initiates the session and streams data to a configured receiver
The device sends SNMP traps on change
The collector polls the device over gNMI
questions.explanation: Dial-out means the device opens the connection, typically gRPC, to the receiver. Dial-in means the collector connects and subscribes, for example with NETCONF or gNMI.

questions.stem: A segment has old switches that cannot export NetFlow, but the team needs flow visibility for it in Secure Network Analytics. What should be added?
options: A Flow Sensor connected to a SPAN or TAP
questions.explanation: The Flow Sensor generates flow records, with application detail, from mirrored traffic. The Flow Collector only receives and stores records that something else exported.

questions.stem: Which capability allows Secure Network Analytics to detect malware in encrypted traffic without decrypting it?
questions.explanation: ETA adds handshake-derived fields, such as the initial data packet and the sequence of packet lengths and times, to flow records. Analytics then classify the traffic without decryption.

questions.stem: A SIEM confirms that an endpoint is beaconing to a known C2 server. Which two components let the SIEM automatically quarantine that endpoint on the network?
options: ISE Adaptive Network Control with CoA
questions.explanation: The SIEM signals ISE over pxGrid. ISE applies an Adaptive Network Control policy and uses Change of Authorization to restrict the session. This is Rapid Threat Containment.

questions.stem: What is the role of pxGrid in the Cisco security ecosystem?
options: It collects posture data from endpoints
It is the publish/subscribe fabric that shares ISE context with other products
It exports NetFlow records to collectors
questions.explanation: ISE is the context broker that knows user, device, posture and location. pxGrid is the certificate-authenticated publish/subscribe fabric that shares that context with FMC, Secure Network Analytics, SIEM and others.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the difference between a SIEM and a SOAR platform?
options: A SIEM blocks traffic inline; a SOAR stores logs
A SIEM correlates events and alerts; a SOAR automates the response with playbooks
They are two names for the same product
A SOAR collects NetFlow; a SIEM collects syslog
questions.explanation: SIEM ingests, normalises and correlates data to raise alerts. SOAR acts on those alerts with automated playbooks such as blocking an IP or quarantining a host.

questions.stem: An analyst must find which internal hosts sent the most traffic to the internet yesterday. Which data source answers this most directly?
questions.explanation: Top talkers and traffic patterns are conversation questions, which is exactly what flow records answer. Telemetry is about live device state.

questions.stem: NetFlow shows one internal host sending nearly 10 MB over UDP/53 to a single external IP in five minutes. What is the most likely explanation?
options: DNS tunneling used for data exfiltration
SNMP polling over the wrong port
questions.explanation: DNS queries are small. A sustained, high-volume UDP/53 conversation to one external host is a classic sign of data being tunneled out over DNS, which objective 6.5 covers.

questions.stem: Which two FMC event types would you check first to see whether FTD blocked an exploit and a malicious download?
questions.explanation: Intrusion events record Snort rule hits such as exploits. File and malware events record file dispositions and malware blocks. Connection and Security Intelligence events are the other two main types.

questions.stem: Why is authenticated NTP considered a security monitoring control?
options: It keeps timestamps trustworthy so events from different devices can be correlated
questions.explanation: Correlation depends on aligned clocks. If an attacker could skew device time, logs would no longer line up, and certificate checks could fail. Authenticated NTP prevents that.

questions.stem: A security audit finds a user port showing "Administrative Mode: dynamic auto" and "Negotiation of Trunking: On". Which attack does this expose?
questions.explanation: A port still running DTP can be negotiated into a trunk by an attacker, which then reaches every VLAN on the switch. That's switch spoofing. Double tagging abuses the native VLAN instead.

questions.stem: Which two commands stop switch-spoofing VLAN hopping on a user access port?
questions.explanation: Hard-coding access mode and disabling DTP negotiation means the port can never become a trunk. The native VLAN, port security and BPDU Guard address other attacks.

questions.stem: Both ends of an inter-switch link are left in dynamic auto. What is the result?
options: The link operates as an access link
questions.explanation: Dynamic auto only responds to DTP; it never initiates. Two auto ports never ask each other, so the link stays access. An attacker who sends desirable DTP to either port still gets a trunk.

questions.stem: Which condition is required for a double-tagging VLAN hopping attack to succeed?
options: The attacker's port runs DTP in desirable mode
The attacker's access port is in the trunk's native VLAN
Port security is set to protect
questions.explanation: The first switch strips the outer tag only because it matches the native VLAN, which is sent untagged on the trunk. The inner tag then delivers the frame into the victim VLAN.

questions.stem: Which two measures defeat double-tagging attacks?
options: Set the trunk native VLAN to an unused VLAN with no access ports
questions.explanation: If no host sits in the native VLAN, nobody can start the attack, and tagging the native VLAN removes the untagged behaviour it relies on.

questions.stem: An engineer changes the native VLAN on one end of a trunk to 999. Which message is expected until the other end is changed?
questions.explanation: CDP compares native VLANs across the link and logs a mismatch (STP also reports inconsistent peer VLAN IDs). Both ends must use the same native VLAN.

questions.stem: A new switch from the lab is connected to production with the same VTP domain and a higher configuration revision. Shortly after, several VLANs disappear across the campus. What is the best preventive control?
options: Run VTP transparent mode or VTPv3 with a primary server
questions.explanation: VTP accepts the database with the highest revision. Transparent mode keeps each switch's VLANs local, and VTPv3 lets only the designated primary server make changes.

questions.stem: An attacker runs macof on a user port. Within seconds the switch begins sending unicast traffic for other hosts to the attacker. Which mechanism is being abused?
questions.explanation: Flooding thousands of random source MACs fills the CAM table. For unknown destinations the switch floods frames out every port in the VLAN, so the attacker can sniff them.

questions.stem: An engineer configures switchport port-security maximum 2 and violation restrict on a port, but show port-security interface reports Port Security: Disabled. What is missing?
questions.explanation: The maximum and violation commands only set parameters. The feature is enabled by the bare switchport port-security command.

questions.stem: A conference room port must stay up during meetings, but security wants a log entry and SNMP trap when extra devices connect. Which violation mode?
questions.explanation: restrict drops frames from MACs beyond the limit, logs, sends a trap and increments the violation counter, without err-disabling the port. protect gives no visibility, and shutdown takes the port down.

questions.stem: Which two statements about port security violation mode shutdown are true?
options: It is the default violation mode
It places the port in err-disabled state
It silently drops frames without logging
It only drops frames from the offending MAC and keeps the port up
It requires errdisable recovery to be configured to work
questions.explanation: shutdown is the default and err-disables the whole port, logging and counting the violation. Recovery can be manual (shut/no shut) or automatic if errdisable recovery is configured.

questions.stem: Which configuration automatically re-enables a port 60 seconds after a port-security violation err-disabled it?
options: errdisable recovery cause psecure-violation and errdisable recovery interval 60
questions.explanation: Err-disable recovery is off by default. Enabling the psecure-violation cause with a 60-second interval brings the port back automatically; if the attack continues, it trips again immediately.

questions.stem: An attacker unplugs a printer and connects a laptop that clones the printer's MAC address. The port uses sticky port security. What happens, and what control would stop it?
options: The port err-disables; no further control needed
Traffic is allowed; 802.1X or MAB with ISE would be needed to verify the device
questions.explanation: Port security counts and pins MAC addresses, but a cloned MAC looks legitimate. Authenticating the device with 802.1X (or MAB plus profiling) addresses identity.

questions.stem: A user connects a small unmanaged-looking switch that sends BPDUs with priority 0 to an access port configured with PortFast. Which feature immediately err-disables that port?
questions.explanation: BPDU Guard err-disables a PortFast edge port as soon as a BPDU arrives. Root Guard would put a port in root-inconsistent state instead of err-disable.

questions.stem: A distribution switch must never accept a new root bridge from the access layer, but STP must keep running on those links. Which feature belongs on the distribution ports facing the access switches?
questions.explanation: Root Guard blocks a port that receives superior BPDUs by placing it in root-inconsistent state, and recovers automatically when they stop. Normal STP operation continues.

questions.stem: Which STP feature should be avoided on ports that could form a loop because it effectively disables spanning tree on the port?
questions.explanation: BPDU Filter stops sending and processing BPDUs, so a loop through that port is not detected. It is used only in narrow, deliberate cases.

questions.stem: Clients in VLAN 40 receive an IP lease with the default gateway 10.40.0.66, an address of a user workstation. Which feature prevents this attack?
questions.explanation: A rogue DHCP server is handing out its own gateway. DHCP snooping drops DHCP server messages (OFFER, ACK) that arrive on untrusted ports.

questions.stem: With DHCP snooping enabled, which port should be configured with ip dhcp snooping trust?
options: Every access port in the snooped VLAN
The uplink toward the legitimate DHCP server or relay
The port connected to the network administrator's PC
questions.explanation: Only the path toward the real DHCP server is trusted. All user ports remain untrusted, the default.

questions.stem: An engineer enters ip dhcp snooping and ip dhcp snooping trust on the uplink, but no bindings appear. Which two things should be checked?
options: ip dhcp snooping vlan includes the user VLAN
Option 82 insertion is not causing the relay or server to drop requests
CDP is enabled on access ports
questions.explanation: Snooping needs the per-VLAN command as well as the global one. When the switch inserts option 82 and an upstream relay or server rejects it, clients get no leases, so no bindings are built.

questions.stem: Which configuration best mitigates a DHCP starvation attack from a single access port?
options: ip dhcp snooping limit rate 10 on the access port plus port security
ip arp inspection trust on the access port
spanning-tree guard root on the access port
questions.explanation: Starvation sends many DHCP requests from random MACs. A snooping rate limit err-disables the port on a flood, and port security caps the number of MACs it can use.

questions.stem: An attacker sends gratuitous ARP replies claiming the gateway's IP address. Which feature drops these replies?
questions.explanation: DAI checks ARP on untrusted ports against the DHCP snooping binding table and drops replies whose IP-to-MAC pair doesn't match a binding.

questions.stem: After enabling DAI on VLAN 50, a file server with a static IP address loses connectivity. What is the best fix?
options: Configure an ARP ACL for the server and apply it with ip arp inspection filter
Set the server port to switchport protected
questions.explanation: Static hosts have no DHCP binding, so DAI drops their ARP. An ARP ACL permitting the server's IP and MAC, applied as a DAI filter, allows it.

questions.stem: What happens by default when an untrusted port exceeds the DAI rate limit?
options: The port is moved to the native VLAN
DAI is disabled for the VLAN
questions.explanation: Untrusted ports allow 15 ARP packets per second by default; exceeding it err-disables the port, which also contains ARP floods.

questions.stem: A host manually configures another user's IP address. Which feature filters its IP packets based on the DHCP snooping binding for that port?
questions.explanation: IP Source Guard (ip verify source) permits only source IPs (and optionally MACs) that match the binding learned on that port.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the dependency between DHCP snooping, DAI and IP Source Guard?
options: DAI builds the binding table that DHCP snooping uses
DHCP snooping builds the binding table that DAI and IP Source Guard validate against
IP Source Guard builds the table for DAI
questions.explanation: DHCP snooping learns MAC, IP, VLAN and port from legitimate leases. DAI uses those bindings to validate ARP, and IPSG uses them to validate IP sources.

questions.stem: A switch port should drop broadcast traffic when it exceeds 20 percent of bandwidth and resume when it falls below 10 percent. Which command?
questions.explanation: The first value is the rising threshold and the second is the falling threshold. Above 20 percent the switch drops broadcast traffic until it falls below 10 percent.

questions.stem: Which two actions should be applied to every unused switch port?
options: Assign it to an unused, unrouted VLAN
Set it as a trunk with native VLAN 1
questions.explanation: Shut the port and park it in a dead VLAN. If someone re-enables it by mistake, it still connects to nothing.

questions.stem: In a private VLAN, which ports can an isolated port communicate with?
options: All ports in the primary VLAN
Other isolated ports and promiscuous ports
questions.explanation: Isolated ports reach only promiscuous ports, typically the gateway or firewall. They cannot reach other isolated ports or community ports.

questions.stem: Several cameras share one subnet and must reach only the default gateway, never each other. Which design fits best on a switch that supports it?
options: Place the cameras on community ports in one community VLAN
Place the cameras on isolated ports and the gateway on a promiscuous port
Put each camera in a separate VLAN and subnet
Enable storm control on the camera ports
questions.explanation: Isolated private VLAN ports keep a single subnet but prevent host-to-host traffic, while all hosts still reach the promiscuous gateway port.

questions.stem: What is a limitation of switchport protected compared with private VLANs?
options: It only works on trunk ports
It only isolates protected ports on the same switch
It blocks access to the default gateway
questions.explanation: Protected ports are locally significant: they stop traffic between protected ports on one switch but don't extend isolation across switches.

questions.stem: Which two statements about Cisco TrustSec Security Group Tags are correct?
options: SGTs can be assigned dynamically through 802.1X or MAB with Cisco ISE
SXP shares IP-to-SGT mappings with devices that cannot tag inline
SGT policy is tied to the switch port where the device connects
questions.explanation: SGTs are role tags assigned by ISE (or statically) and propagated inline or via SXP. Policy follows the role, not the port or VLAN, and is enforced with SGACLs.

questions.stem: Contractors must never reach finance servers anywhere across three campuses, regardless of where either connects. Which segmentation approach scales best?
options: Private VLANs on every access switch
Security Group Tags with SGACL policy managed in ISE
questions.explanation: Identity-based tags follow the device and are enforced by a central policy matrix, so the rule holds across locations without per-port or per-IP configuration.

questions.stem: Why should CDP be disabled on user-facing ports?
options: It leaks device model, IOS version, management IP and native VLAN to anyone listening
questions.explanation: CDP and LLDP give an attacker free reconnaissance. Keep them where operations need them (infrastructure links, IP phones) and turn them off toward hosts.

questions.stem: An access port with PortFast and BPDU Guard goes err-disabled when a user connects a small switch. The switch has been removed. What restores the port?
options: Nothing: the port recovers automatically when BPDUs stop
Enter shutdown and then no shutdown on the interface
Enter no spanning-tree bpduguard enable on the interface
questions.explanation: BPDU Guard err-disables the port, and an err-disabled port stays down until it is bounced with shutdown and no shutdown (or an errdisable recovery timer fires). Removing BPDU Guard would just remove the protection.

questions.stem: A distribution switch is the root for VLAN 10 at priority 4096 and has Root Guard on its downlink Fa0/10. A switch with priority 0 is connected to Fa0/10. What happens?
options: The new switch becomes root and Fa0/10 becomes a root port
Fa0/10 is err-disabled until an administrator bounces it
Fa0/10 is placed in root-inconsistent state and recovers by itself when the superior BPDUs stop
The distribution switch lowers its own priority to 0
questions.explanation: Root Guard blocks the port as root-inconsistent while superior BPDUs arrive and returns it to forwarding automatically when they stop. It never err-disables the port, and STP never changes a configured priority by itself.

questions.stem: After DHCP snooping is enabled for VLAN 10, no client gets a lease. The uplink toward the IOS router acting as DHCP server is trusted, and the router is in the same VLAN. What is the most likely fix?
options: Enter no ip dhcp snooping information option on the switch
Disable ip dhcp snooping vlan 10 and enable it globally only
Configure ip arp inspection trust on the uplink
questions.explanation: The switch inserts option 82 with a giaddr of 0.0.0.0 by default, and an IOS DHCP server drops those requests. Stop the insertion on the switch, or configure ip dhcp relay information trust-all on the server. Trusting access ports would let rogue servers answer.

questions.stem: A trunk connects a distribution switch (the STP root) to an access switch. Which two placements are correct?
options: Root Guard on the distribution switch port facing the access switch
Root Guard on the access switch port facing the distribution switch
Loop Guard on the access switch root port facing the distribution switch
BPDU Guard on both ends of the trunk
Root Guard and Loop Guard together on the access switch uplink
questions.explanation: Root Guard belongs on the root's downlinks, where a superior BPDU should never appear. Loop Guard protects a root or alternate port that could stop receiving BPDUs. The two can't share a port, and BPDU Guard on a trunk would shut the link down.

questions.stem: An interface has storm-control broadcast level 1.00 0.50 and storm-control action shutdown. Broadcast traffic reaches 3 percent of bandwidth. What happens?
options: Excess broadcast is dropped and the port stays up
A trap is sent and all traffic is still forwarded
questions.explanation: With action shutdown, crossing the rising threshold err-disables the port. Without an action, excess traffic of that type is simply dropped until it falls below the falling threshold; action trap adds a log message and SNMP trap.

questions.stem: A company runs one FTD at a small branch with no central IT team. Which management option fits best?
questions.explanation: One FTD with no central team is the case FDM is built for: an on-box manager for a single device. A central manager adds cost and complexity without benefit here.

questions.stem: An organization has ASAs, FTDs and Meraki MX appliances across 120 sites, and administrators work remotely. They want one place to manage security policy. Which solution fits best?
questions.explanation: Security Cloud Control is cloud-based and manages ASA, FTD (through cloud-delivered FMC) and Meraki MX from one interface, reachable from anywhere. The other options manage one device or one platform.

questions.stem: Which product is Security Cloud Control the evolution of?
questions.explanation: Security Cloud Control evolved from Cisco Defense Orchestrator (CDO), and Cisco documentation and licensing still use the CDO name in places.

questions.stem: A security team must still be able to reach its firewalls while a DDoS attack saturates the production network. Which design meets this requirement?
options: In-band management over the data interfaces
Out-of-band management on a separate management network
questions.explanation: In-band management shares the production network, so it fails with it. An out-of-band path is separate, so it stays available during the outage.

questions.stem: Which two statements about on-premises management with FMC compared with cloud management through Security Cloud Control are true?
options: On-premises management keeps management data on the organization's network
Cloud management requires the organization to patch and upgrade the management platform
On-premises management can be reached from anywhere without a VPN by design
Cloud management depends on internet connectivity
On-premises management removes all maintenance work
questions.explanation: On-premises keeps data local but leaves maintenance to you. Cloud management is maintained by Cisco and reachable from anywhere, but it depends on internet access.

questions.stem: An ASA in a data center can't be reached directly from Security Cloud Control. What lets SCC manage it?
options: A Secure Device Connector on the local network
Enabling ASDM on the outside interface
Registering the ASA to an on-premises FMC
questions.explanation: A Secure Device Connector is a small VM on the customer network that relays between Security Cloud Control and devices the cloud can't reach directly. Exposing ASDM on the outside interface would weaken security.

questions.stem: An administrator changes an ASA rule directly with the CLI, bypassing Security Cloud Control. Which SCC capability highlights this?
questions.explanation: Out-of-band change detection flags changes made directly on the device so they can be accepted or rejected, which is how SCC catches configuration drift.

questions.stem: Which statement about managing an FTD is true?
options: An FTD can be managed by FDM and FMC at the same time
FDM manages many FTDs from one console
An FTD is managed by either FDM or FMC, and FMC manages many devices
ASDM is the multidevice manager for FTD
questions.explanation: FDM is on-box management for a single FTD; FMC (on-prem or cloud-delivered) manages many. A device uses one or the other. ASDM is for ASA.

questions.stem: What is a CIS Benchmark?
options: A vendor-specific performance test for firewalls
A consensus-based set of secure configuration recommendations for a specific technology
An organization-wide list of prioritized security safeguards
A vulnerability scanner published by the Center for Internet Security
questions.explanation: A CIS Benchmark is a consensus-based configuration guide for one product. The organization-wide list of safeguards is the CIS Controls.

questions.stem: A CIS Benchmark recommendation is marked Level 2. What does that indicate?
options: It provides defense in depth and may reduce functionality or performance
It applies only to cloud platforms
It is optional and has no security benefit
questions.explanation: Level 2 extends Level 1 for environments where security is paramount, and it may affect functionality or performance. Manual vs. automated is a separate attribute.

questions.stem: Which two benefits are reasons to adopt CIS Benchmarks?
options: They standardize secure configuration across devices
They remove the need for patching
They support compliance with frameworks such as PCI DSS
They replace the need for a firewall
They guarantee devices cannot be compromised
questions.explanation: Benchmarks reduce attack surface, prevent misconfiguration, standardize configuration and support compliance. They don't replace patching or other controls.

questions.stem: Which part of a CIS Benchmark recommendation tells you how to check whether a device is compliant?
questions.explanation: The audit procedure is the command or check that proves compliance. Remediation is how to fix it; rationale is why; impact is what it might break.

questions.stem: The CIS Benchmarks for Cisco IOS XE group their recommendations how?
options: By management, control and data plane
questions.explanation: The Cisco network-device benchmarks follow the three planes: management (AAA, SSH, SNMPv3, NTP, logging), control (routing authentication) and data (uRPF, ACLs).

questions.stem: A team hardened 80 firewalls to a CIS baseline last year. An audit now finds Telnet enabled on several. What is this called, and what prevents it from going unnoticed?
options: Configuration drift; regular audits and change detection
questions.explanation: Changes that move a device away from its approved baseline are configuration drift. Regular audits, change logs and out-of-band change detection catch it so it can be remediated.

questions.stem: Where is most CIS-style management-plane hardening applied on Cisco Secure Firewall Threat Defense?
options: In the FTD expert-mode Linux shell
In platform settings pushed from the management center
In the access control policy's default action
questions.explanation: FTD management-plane settings such as SSH and HTTPS access, external authentication, syslog, SNMP and NTP live in platform settings deployed from FMC (or FDM / Security Cloud Control).

questions.stem: Which two statements about TACACS+ are true?
options: It separates authentication, authorization and accounting
It is the preferred protocol for 802.1X network access
questions.explanation: TACACS+ runs over TCP 49, encrypts the whole body and separates the three AAA functions, which enables per-command authorization. UDP 1812/1813, password-only hiding and 802.1X describe RADIUS.

questions.stem: An administrator configures aaa authentication login VTY group tacacs+ local. The TACACS+ server is reachable but rejects the user's password. What happens?
options: The router tries the local database
Authentication fails; the local database is not tried
The router retries the server until it accepts
The user is logged in at privilege level 1
questions.explanation: The next method is used only when the current one returns an error, such as no server answering. A reject from a reachable server is final.

questions.stem: debug tacacs shows Opened TCP/IP handle to the server, followed by received bad AUTHEN packet and Invalid AUTHEN/START/LOGIN/ASCII packet (check keys). What is the cause?
options: The shared key does not match
The method list is not applied
questions.explanation: The TCP connection opened, so the server is reachable. A reply that fails to decrypt points to a shared key mismatch.

questions.stem: test aaa group tacacs+ admin1 Pass legacy succeeds, but VTY logins never appear in debug tacacs and authenticate against the local database. What is the most likely cause?
options: The method list is not applied to the VTY lines, or its name doesn't match
questions.explanation: test aaa talks to the server group directly and ignores line configuration. A working test with a silent debug on real logins means the method list isn't bound to the lines.

questions.stem: A router pings the TACACS+ server successfully, but test aaa reports No authoritative response from any server and debug tacacs shows a connection timeout. What should the engineer check?
options: The shared key on the router
Whether an ACL or firewall blocks TCP port 49
The user's password on the server
questions.explanation: A connection timeout is a reachability failure. Ping uses ICMP and proves nothing about TCP 49, which a filter may still block.

questions.stem: After aaa new-model and a TACACS+ login list are configured, users log in successfully but cannot enter privileged EXEC mode. What is a valid fix?
options: Configure enable secret or aaa authentication enable
Remove the local keyword from the method list
questions.explanation: Authentication doesn't grant privilege; users land at level 1. An enable secret, enable authentication against the server, or exec authorization returning privilege 15 fixes it.

questions.stem: Which protocol should be used for per-command authorization of network administrators?
questions.explanation: TACACS+ separates authorization from authentication, so the device can ask the server about each command. RADIUS combines authentication and authorization.

questions.stem: 802.1X authentication succeeds in ISE, but the switch never places the endpoint in the VLAN that ISE returns. What is missing on the switch?
questions.explanation: aaa authorization network lets the switch apply authorization attributes from the RADIUS server, such as a VLAN, downloadable ACL or SGT.

questions.stem: ISE changes an endpoint's authorization policy, but the switch keeps the old access until the endpoint reconnects. What should be configured?
options: aaa server radius dynamic-author with ISE as a client
questions.explanation: Change of Authorization lets ISE reauthenticate or reassign a live session. On IOS it's enabled with aaa server radius dynamic-author.

questions.stem: A switch's RADIUS shared key was mistyped. What does the switch most likely observe?
options: Access-Reject with a clear key-mismatch message
Timeouts or replies it discards, while the server log shows the real reason
No effect, because RADIUS keys are optional
questions.explanation: RADIUS is connectionless and validated with the shared secret, so a key mismatch usually looks like timeouts from the device. The server's log, such as ISE Live Logs, identifies the real cause.

questions.stem: A TACACS+ server was fixed after an outage, but logins still go straight to the local fallback for several minutes. What explains this?
options: The server is marked dead and skipped for the dead-time
The method list name is misspelled
questions.explanation: After repeated failures IOS marks a server dead and skips it for the dead-time window. show aaa servers shows the state.

questions.stem: Which two RADIUS characteristics are true?
options: It encrypts the entire packet body
questions.explanation: RADIUS uses UDP 1812 (and 1813 for accounting), hides only the password, and returns authentication and authorization together in one Access-Accept.
